chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Rub the palates of your children with the clay of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for verily it is protection.

key_terms.أَمَانٌ: Protection, safety, or security from harm
key_terms.تُرْبَةِ: Clay or earth, specifically referring to the soil from the grave
key_terms.حَنِّكُوا: Rub the palate (of a newborn) with something sweet or blessed

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of rubbing a newborn's palate with the clay of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia practice of using the clay from Imam al-Husayn’s grave as a spiritual safeguard for newborns, linking physical ritual to metaphysical protection. It underscores the concept of *tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, where the martyr’s sacrifice serves as an enduring source of divine mercy and security for the faithful.
